elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: "Client may assign or transfer this Agreement without approval to an affiliate..." — express, unconditional, no approval required.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: "...or to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all of its assets" without approval — all three trigger events named.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall not assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without Client's prior written approval"; the former mutual "financially responsible affiliate" exception no longer applies to TrueLink, so no residual no-consent Vendor route remains.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "...without Client's prior written approval, which shall not be unreasonably withheld".

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: "...and shall never assign to a Client competitor" — absolute bar, not merely a consent factor.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: "...no change of control of Client shall give TrueLink any right to terminate this Agreement"; no contrary retained termination trigger in Section 15.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: Only Client is given a successor right; TrueLink's assignments (including to a successor) still require Client's prior written approval, so the mutual successor construct is absent.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: The Client successor carve-out is silent on notice; no written-notice obligation appears anywhere in the rendered clause.
Client retains a no-consent, non-successor affiliate exception ("without approval to an affiliate"), which by the ASSIGN fallback boundary defeats "other assignments require consent".

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: For the only assignments that still require consent (TrueLink's), the clause states approval "shall not be unreasonably withheld".

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all six preferred elements appear in operative language (one-way consent on TrueLink with a reasonableness standard, absolute competitor bar, Client affiliate and successor carve-outs, and an express no-change-of-control-termination confirmation).

Fallback is not independently satisfied (no Vendor successor right, no written-notice mechanic, retained Client affiliate no-consent exception), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is complete.

Minimal: the only deletion outside the added text is the mutual "financially responsible affiliate" exception, whose removal on the Vendor side is strictly required by the preferred element "Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent." No survival tails, procedures, notice mechanics, or other extras were added; each added phrase maps to a listed preferred element.

Preserves intent: the clause remains a single assignment provision, the Customer-side rights are implemented by a direct "without approval" permission rather than a broad notwithstanding override or a new Vendor assignment exception, and no undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence results.
Drafter note for completeness: the change-of-control sentence is confirmatory only (no such Vendor right existed), which is consistent with the margin comment and does not create inconsistency.
